game.name: Catan
game.description: Trade resources, build roads and settlements, and become the first to ten victory points on the island of Catan.
game.objective: Be the first player to reach 10 victory points by building settlements, cities, and roads, or by holding special cards.

setupSteps.title: Build the island
setupSteps.body: Arrange the 19 hex tiles randomly inside the frame. Place the sea frame pieces around the edge.
setupSteps.tip: For your first game, use the recommended layout in the rulebook so resources are balanced.

setupSteps.title: Place number tokens
setupSteps.body: Lay the round number tokens on the hexes in alphabetical order (A, B, C...). Skip the desert hex.

images.caption: Number tokens go on hexes clockwise

setupSteps.title: Place the robber
setupSteps.body: Set the robber pawn on the desert hex.

setupSteps.title: Hand out player kits
setupSteps.body: Each player takes 5 settlements, 4 cities, 15 roads, and one building costs card in their color.

setupSteps.title: Initial placement
setupSteps.body: In player order, each player places one settlement and one connecting road. Then in reverse order, each player places a second settlement and road.
setupSteps.tip: Pick spots that touch three different resources for the strongest start.

setupSteps.title: Collect starting resources
setupSteps.body: For the second settlement, take one resource card for each adjacent hex.

images.caption: Take cards for the 3 adjacent hexes

howToPlaySteps.title: What happens on a turn
howToPlaySteps.body: A turn has three phases: roll for resources, trade, and build. You may build at any point during your turn after rolling.

rules.title: Roll the dice
rules.body: Total the two dice. Every player gets resources from hexes with that number that touch their settlements or cities.

rules.title: Trade
rules.body: Trade resources with other players or with the bank (4:1, or 3:1 / 2:1 at ports).

rules.title: Build
rules.body: Spend resources to build roads, settlements, cities, or buy development cards.

howToPlaySteps.title: Rolling a 7
howToPlaySteps.body: Rolling a 7 triggers the robber. Players with more than 7 cards must discard half. The roller moves the robber to a new hex and steals one card from a player touching it.
howToPlaySteps.warning: If you sit on a pile of cards, expect to lose half of them when someone rolls a 7.

turnFlow.name: Roll dice
turnFlow.description: Distribute resources based on the rolled number.

turnFlow.name: Trade
turnFlow.description: Trade with other players or with the bank.

turnFlow.name: Build
turnFlow.description: Spend resources to expand your network or buy a development card.

scoring.summary: Victory points are earned by building and by holding special cards. First to 10 on your turn wins.
points: Victory Point development cards: 1 VP each
scoring.tieBreaker: The current player declares 10+ VP first, so there is no tie.
scoring.gameEnd: The game ends the moment a player declares 10 or more victory points at the start of their turn.

faq.question: Can I count hidden VP cards toward winning?
faq.answer: Yes, but you only reveal them on the turn you would win.

faq.question: Can two settlements be next to each other?
faq.answer: No. Settlements must be at least two roads apart.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting to collect on opponents' rolls
commonMistakes.body: Every player collects on every roll, not just the active player.

commonMistakes.title: Trading on someone else's turn
commonMistakes.body: You can only trade with the active player, not with other players directly.

game.name: Ticket to Ride
game.description: Collect train cards and claim railway routes across the map to connect cities on your tickets.
game.objective: Score the most points by claiming routes, completing destination tickets, and holding the longest continuous train line.

setupSteps.title: Place the board
setupSteps.body: Unfold the board where everyone can reach the routes you plan to claim.

setupSteps.title: Shuffle and deal trains
setupSteps.body: Each player picks a color and takes 45 train pieces and the matching scoring marker. Place markers on 0.

setupSteps.title: Deal train cards
setupSteps.body: Shuffle the train deck, deal 4 cards to each player, and reveal 5 face-up next to the deck.

images.caption: Start with 4 train cards; 5 face-up market

setupSteps.title: Deal destination tickets
setupSteps.body: Give each player 3 destination tickets. They must keep at least 2.
setupSteps.tip: Tickets that overlap in geography are easier to complete together.
setupSteps.warning: Failing to complete a kept ticket subtracts its points at the end.

howToPlaySteps.title: Choose one action per turn
howToPlaySteps.body: On your turn, do exactly one of these three actions.

rules.title: Draw train cards
rules.body: Take two train cards. Face-up locomotives count as two cards, so you only get one.

rules.title: Claim a route
rules.body: Spend train cards matching the route's color and length to place trains on it.

rules.title: Draw destination tickets
rules.body: Draw 3 new tickets and keep at least 1.

turnFlow.name: Pick an action
turnFlow.description: Draw, claim, or take tickets — only one per turn.

turnFlow.name: Resolve effect
turnFlow.description: Score immediately if you claimed a route.

turnFlow.name: End turn
turnFlow.description: Play passes to the left.

scoring.summary: Score points for routes you claim, completed tickets, and the longest continuous track.
scoring.gameEnd: When a player ends their turn with 2 or fewer trains left, every player takes one final turn.

faq.question: Can I split my hand to claim a route?
faq.answer: No, you must use one valid set of matching cards in a single action.

commonMistakes.title: Hoarding cards too long
commonMistakes.body: Other players can claim the routes you need first.

game.name: Codenames
game.description: Two teams race to identify their secret agents using one-word clues from their spymaster.
game.objective: Find all your team's agents from a 5x5 grid before the other team — and avoid the assassin.

setupSteps.title: Form two teams
setupSteps.body: Split into red and blue teams of roughly equal size. Each team picks one spymaster.

setupSteps.title: Lay out the words
setupSteps.body: Shuffle the word cards and place 25 face up in a 5x5 grid.

setupSteps.title: Pick a key card
setupSteps.body: Spymasters draw a random key card and place it on the stand. Both spymasters keep the key card hidden from their team.
setupSteps.warning: Do not let the team see the key card or your reactions to it.

images.caption: Key card stays hidden from teammates

howToPlaySteps.title: Spymaster gives a clue
howToPlaySteps.body: On your team's turn, the spymaster says a one-word clue and a number — for example: "Beach 2". The clue must relate to that many of your team's words.

rules.title: One word, one number
rules.body: Clues must be one word and a number. No proper nouns from the grid.

rules.title: Touch a card to guess
rules.body: Teammates touch a card to lock in a guess. The spymaster reveals what it is.

rules.title: Stop or continue
rules.body: After each correct guess, the team may guess again up to one more than the number. End turn anytime.

turnFlow.name: Give clue
turnFlow.description: Spymaster announces a one-word clue and a number.

turnFlow.name: Guess
turnFlow.description: Teammates discuss and tap cards one at a time.

turnFlow.name: Resolve
turnFlow.description: Correct cards are covered with the matching agent. Wrong guesses end the turn.

scoring.summary: Find all your agents first to win. Touching the assassin loses the game instantly.
points: Each correct guess covers one agent
First team to cover all their agents wins

faq.question: Can the clue rhyme with a word on the table?
faq.answer: House rule, but the standard rules say no.

commonMistakes.title: Going for too many words
commonMistakes.body: Big numbers feel impressive but a vague clue can hit the assassin.

sections.title: End game
items: All your agents found → you win

game.name: Pandemic
game.description: Work together as a global response team to treat outbreaks and discover cures before the world is overwhelmed.
game.objective: Discover cures for all four diseases before the player deck runs out or eight outbreaks occur.

setupSteps.title: Place the board
setupSteps.body: Set the world map in the middle of the table within reach of everyone.

setupSteps.title: Deal roles
setupSteps.body: Each player gets a random role card and pawn. Place all pawns on Atlanta.

images.caption: Each player has a unique role

setupSteps.title: Build infection deck
setupSteps.body: Shuffle the infection cards. Place 3 sets of 3 cards on cities to seed initial outbreaks following the rulebook (3 cubes, 2 cubes, 1 cube).

setupSteps.title: Build player deck
setupSteps.body: Shuffle the player cards. Deal a starting hand based on player count (4 cards for 2P, 3 for 3P, 2 for 4P). Then split deck into piles and shuffle in epidemic cards.
setupSteps.tip: More epidemic cards = harder game. 4 is standard, 5 or 6 for veterans.

howToPlaySteps.title: On your turn, do 4 actions
howToPlaySteps.body: Pick from move, fly, build research station, treat disease, share knowledge, or discover a cure.

rules.title: Take 4 actions
rules.body: Mix and match the available actions as you wish.

rules.title: Draw 2 player cards
rules.body: If you draw an Epidemic, resolve it immediately.

rules.title: Infect cities
rules.body: Flip the top X infection cards (X = current infection rate) and add a cube to each city.

turnFlow.name: 4 actions
turnFlow.description: Take any 4 actions in any order.

turnFlow.name: Draw player cards
turnFlow.description: Draw 2 player cards. Resolve epidemics immediately.

turnFlow.name: Infect cities
turnFlow.description: Infect cities equal to the current infection rate.

scoring.summary: There is no score. The team wins by discovering all four cures.
scoring.gameEnd: You lose if 8 outbreaks happen, you run out of disease cubes of a color, or the player deck runs out before all cures are found.

faq.question: Do we have to eradicate diseases to win?
faq.answer: No, you only need to cure them. Eradication is a strong bonus.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting outbreaks chain
commonMistakes.body: An outbreak in a city causes infections in neighbors, which can chain further.

sections.title: Actions
items: Discover a cure (5 matching cards at a station)

sections.title: Losing conditions
items: Out of disease cubes for a color

game.name: Wingspan
game.description: Attract birds to your wildlife reserves in this engine-building card game inspired by nature.
game.objective: Score the most points by laying eggs, gaining food, drawing cards, and triggering end-of-round goals.

setupSteps.title: Give each player a mat
setupSteps.body: Place a player mat in front of each player. The three habitats run from top to bottom.

setupSteps.title: Deal starting hands
setupSteps.body: Deal 5 bird cards and 2 bonus cards to each player. Players keep some and discard the rest, then take a matching pool of starting food.

setupSteps.title: Fill the bird tray
setupSteps.body: Reveal 3 bird cards face up next to the deck. Place the food dice in the bird feeder dome and roll them in.

images.caption: Food dice in the feeder dome

howToPlaySteps.title: Take one action per turn
howToPlaySteps.body: On your turn pick one of the four habitats. Carry out its action, then trigger any powers in that habitat from right to left.

rules.title: Play a bird
rules.body: Spend food and eggs to place a bird in the matching habitat.

rules.title: Gain food
rules.body: Take dice from the bird feeder, then trigger forest powers.

rules.title: Lay eggs
rules.body: Add eggs to your birds, then trigger grassland powers.

rules.title: Draw bird cards
rules.body: Take face-up or top of deck, then trigger wetland powers.

turnFlow.name: Pick a habitat
turnFlow.description: Choose forest, grassland, or wetland — or play a bird.

turnFlow.name: Take the action
turnFlow.description: Gain the listed resource based on the habitat's cubes.

turnFlow.name: Trigger powers
turnFlow.description: Resolve bird powers in that row from right to left.

scoring.summary: Add points from birds, bonus cards, end-of-round goals, eggs, food cached on birds, and tucked cards.
points: Food cached on birds (1 pt each)

faq.question: Can I play more than one bird per turn?
faq.answer: Only with bird powers that explicitly allow it.

commonMistakes.title: Skipping bird powers
commonMistakes.body: Always trigger right-to-left powers in the row you played in.

game.name: Chess
game.description: The classic two-player strategy game of pure skill on a 64-square board.
game.objective: Checkmate the opponent's king — put it under attack with no legal escape.

components.name: Pieces per player
components.description: 1 king, 1 queen, 2 rooks, 2 bishops, 2 knights, 8 pawns

setupSteps.title: Orient the board
setupSteps.body: Each player should have a light square on their bottom-right corner.

setupSteps.title: Place the pieces
setupSteps.body: Pawns go on the second rank. Rooks at the corners, then knights, then bishops, then queen on her color, king on the last square.

howToPlaySteps.title: How pieces move
howToPlaySteps.body: Each piece has its own movement rule. You can only land on empty squares or capture an opposing piece.

rules.title: Pawn
rules.body: Moves forward 1 (or 2 from its starting square). Captures diagonally.

rules.title: Knight
rules.body: L-shape: 2 squares one direction then 1 perpendicular. Jumps over pieces.

rules.title: Bishop / Rook / Queen
rules.body: Bishop: diagonals. Rook: ranks and files. Queen: any straight line.

rules.title: King
rules.body: Moves one square in any direction. Cannot move into check.

howToPlaySteps.title: Special moves
howToPlaySteps.body: Castling, en passant, and promotion add depth to the basic moves.
howToPlaySteps.warning: You cannot castle through or out of check.

turnFlow.name: Plan your move
turnFlow.description: Look for threats against your king first, then yours against theirs.

turnFlow.name: Move one piece
turnFlow.description: Make exactly one legal move, capturing if you wish.

turnFlow.name: Press the clock (optional)
turnFlow.description: If using a clock, press it to end your turn.

scoring.summary: There is no score. The game ends in checkmate, stalemate, resignation, or a draw.
scoring.gameEnd: Checkmate ends the game. Stalemate, threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, or insufficient material end in a draw.

faq.question: Can a pawn promote to any piece?
faq.answer: Yes, including a second queen. Most often promoted to queen.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring development
commonMistakes.body: Move several pieces in the opening rather than the same piece twice.

game.name: Carcassonne
game.description: Draw and place landscape tiles to build a medieval countryside, then claim roads, cities, and fields with your meeples.
game.objective: Score the most points by completing roads, cities, monasteries, and farms.

components.name: Land tiles
components.description: Includes one start tile with a dark back

setupSteps.title: Place the start tile
setupSteps.body: Put the dark-backed start tile in the middle of the table. All other tiles will branch from here.

setupSteps.title: Shuffle the tile pile
setupSteps.body: Stack the remaining tiles face down in a few piles within easy reach.

setupSteps.title: Hand out meeples
setupSteps.body: Each player takes 7 meeples in one color. One meeple goes on the 0 of the scoring board.

howToPlaySteps.title: Three steps on your turn
howToPlaySteps.body: Draw a tile, place it so edges match, then optionally place a meeple on it.

rules.title: Draw a tile
rules.body: Take one tile from a pile and reveal it to everyone.

rules.title: Place it legally
rules.body: The tile must touch at least one existing tile and match all shared edges.

rules.title: Place a meeple (optional)
rules.body: Put one of your meeples on the tile you just placed — as a knight, robber, monk, or farmer. The feature must be unclaimed.

howToPlaySteps.title: Score completed features
howToPlaySteps.body: Roads close when both ends are capped. Cities close when fully walled. Monasteries score when surrounded by 8 tiles.
howToPlaySteps.warning: Once a feature is scored, take your meeple back. Farmers stay on the board until the very end of the game.

turnFlow.name: Draw tile
turnFlow.description: Reveal one tile from a face-down pile.

turnFlow.name: Place tile
turnFlow.description: Edges must match. The tile must touch an existing tile.

turnFlow.name: Place meeple (optional)
turnFlow.description: Claim an unclaimed feature on the new tile.

scoring.summary: Score completed features mid-game; score uncompleted features and farms at the end.
points: City: 2 pts per tile + 2 pts per pennant
Monastery: 9 pts when surrounded by 8 tiles (incl. its own)
Farm (end of game): 3 pts per completed city the farm feeds
scoring.tieBreaker: Ties stand — multiple winners is fine.
scoring.gameEnd: The game ends when the last tile is placed. Then score all unfinished features and farms.

faq.question: Can I place a meeple on a feature an opponent already claimed?
faq.answer: Not directly. But if two roads or cities merge later, both meeples score it.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting to retrieve meeples
commonMistakes.body: When a feature scores, your meeple comes back to your supply for reuse.

sections.title: Scoring during play
items: City: 2 pts per tile + 2 per pennant

sections.title: End-of-game scoring
items: Incomplete road/city: 1 pt per tile / 1 per pennant
Farmer: 3 pts per fed completed city

game.name: Splendor
game.description: Collect gem tokens to buy prestige cards and become the most renowned Renaissance jewel merchant.
game.objective: Be the first player to reach 15 prestige points.

setupSteps.title: Lay out the gem tokens
setupSteps.body: Stack the 5 gem colors and the gold tokens in piles within reach of all players.

setupSteps.title: Build the 3 card rows
setupSteps.body: Shuffle each development deck separately. Reveal 4 cards from each tier so there are 3 rows of 4 face up.

setupSteps.title: Draw nobles
setupSteps.body: Reveal (player count + 1) noble tiles. The rest go back in the box.

howToPlaySteps.title: Choose one action per turn
howToPlaySteps.body: On your turn do exactly one of: take gems, reserve a card, or buy a card. Then check if a noble visits you.

rules.title: Take gems
rules.body: Take 3 different-colored tokens, or 2 of the same color (only if the pile has 4+).

rules.title: Reserve a card
rules.body: Take a face-up or top-of-deck card into a hidden hand of up to 3, and gain one gold token.

rules.title: Buy a card
rules.body: Pay the cost in gems and previously bought cards (which act as permanent discounts). Replace the slot.

turnFlow.name: Pick action
turnFlow.description: Take gems, reserve, or buy.

turnFlow.name: Refill / check
turnFlow.description: Refill the card row. Check the noble row for visits.

turnFlow.name: Discard down to 10
turnFlow.description: If you hold more than 10 gem tokens, return the excess to the bank.

scoring.summary: Score prestige points from purchased cards and noble visits.
points: Each bought card: its printed prestige (often 0-5)
First to 15 prestige triggers the final round
scoring.gameEnd: When a player reaches 15 prestige on their turn, finish the current round so everyone has the same number of turns. Most prestige wins.

faq.question: Can a noble visit on someone else's turn?
faq.answer: Yes — but only one noble per turn, and visits only happen at the end of the active player's turn.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting the 10-token cap
commonMistakes.body: Returning excess tokens at end of turn is mandatory, not optional.

sections.title: Actions (pick one)
items: Take 2 of the same (pile must have 4+)

sections.title: Discounts
items: Each bought card permanently reduces future costs of its color by 1

game.name: Azul
game.description: Decorate the walls of the Royal Palace of Évora by drafting beautiful Portuguese tiles row by row.
game.objective: Score the most points by carefully placing tiles on your wall to form sets, columns, and rows.

setupSteps.title: Place factory displays
setupSteps.body: Put (2 × players + 1) factory displays in a circle on the table. Fill each with 4 random tiles from the bag.

setupSteps.title: Hand out player boards
setupSteps.body: Each player takes a board and a scoring marker placed on 0.

setupSteps.title: Choose start player
setupSteps.body: The player who most recently visited Portugal goes first. Place the first-player marker in the center pool.

howToPlaySteps.title: Drafting tiles
howToPlaySteps.body: Take all tiles of one color from a factory display; remaining tiles go to the center pool. Or take all tiles of one color from the center.

rules.title: Pick a source
rules.body: Either a factory display or the center pool.

rules.title: Take one color
rules.body: All tiles of that color go to your pattern lines. Other factory tiles slide to the center.

rules.title: Overflow drops to your floor
rules.body: Tiles that don't fit on a pattern line go onto your floor line — and they cost you negative points.

howToPlaySteps.title: Wall tiling phase
howToPlaySteps.body: At the end of the round, complete pattern lines move ONE tile to the matching column on your wall; the rest go to the lid.
howToPlaySteps.warning: Incomplete pattern lines stay where they are — they keep the tiles you've drafted.

images.caption: Place tile on wall, score adjacent tiles

turnFlow.name: Draft
turnFlow.description: Take one color from a factory or the center.

turnFlow.name: Stage on pattern lines
turnFlow.description: Place on the rightmost-fitting pattern line, overflow to floor.

turnFlow.name: End-of-round tiling
turnFlow.description: Move one tile per completed pattern line to the wall and score.

scoring.summary: Score every wall tile you place during the tiling phase, then take penalties from your floor line.
points: Wall tile in a row/column: count all connected tiles (incl. itself)
End-game bonuses: 2 pts per full row, 7 pts per full column, 10 pts per complete color set
scoring.gameEnd: The game ends the round a player completes any horizontal row on their wall.

faq.question: What if I can't legally place tiles on any pattern line?
faq.answer: They all go to the floor line as penalties.

commonMistakes.title: Filling a pattern line you already have on the wall
commonMistakes.body: You cannot. Drafting that color forces tiles onto the floor instead.

game.name: 7 Wonders
game.description: Lead an ancient civilization across three ages by simultaneously drafting cards to build your wonder, military, science, and economy.
game.objective: Have the most victory points after three ages of card drafting.

components.name: Wonder boards
components.description: Each has an A and B side

components.name: Age I / II / III card decks

setupSteps.title: Give each player a Wonder
setupSteps.body: Deal each player one Wonder board, A or B side up. Each starts with 3 coins.

setupSteps.title: Prepare Age I
setupSteps.body: Shuffle Age I cards. Deal each player 7 cards face-down. Remove unused Guild cards based on player count for Ages I and II.
checklist: Age I deck shuffled and dealt

howToPlaySteps.title: Simultaneous drafting
howToPlaySteps.body: Each age has 6 rounds. Every round, every player picks one card from their hand and passes the rest in the age's direction (Age I and III: left; Age II: right).

rules.title: Build a structure
rules.body: Pay the cost in resources or coins. The card stays in front of you.

rules.title: Build a Wonder stage
rules.body: Tuck the card under your Wonder board, paying the listed cost.

rules.title: Sell for coins
rules.body: Discard the card to gain 3 coins.

howToPlaySteps.title: End-of-age combat
howToPlaySteps.body: After the 6 rounds of each age, neighbors compare shield (military) counts. The higher count earns conflict tokens; the lower one loses a -1 token.
howToPlaySteps.warning: Conflict tokens give +1 / +3 / +5 in Ages I / II / III. Falling behind costs you.

turnFlow.name: Choose a card
turnFlow.description: All players pick one card from their hand simultaneously.

turnFlow.name: Resolve the card
turnFlow.description: Build a structure, build a Wonder stage, or discard for 3 coins.

turnFlow.name: Pass the hand
turnFlow.description: Hand the rest to the neighbor in the age's direction.

scoring.summary: Add up points from civilian, military, science, commercial, guild cards, Wonder stages, and treasury.
points: Science: sets of identical symbols + groups of 3 different (7 pts per group)
Guild (purple): variable, set in Age III
scoring.gameEnd: After Age III's 6 rounds and the final conflict resolution, total each player's points. Most points wins.

faq.question: Can I build a card I already have?
faq.answer: No — duplicate structures are illegal. But many cards let you build later ones for free.

commonMistakes.title: Ignoring resource diversity
commonMistakes.body: Without raw goods, you'll be forced to pay neighbors or discard cards for coins.

game.name: King of Tokyo
game.description: Become a giant monster smashing your way through Tokyo — roll dice, attack rivals, and claim victory.
game.objective: Be the last monster standing or be the first to 20 victory points.

setupSteps.title: Pick a monster
setupSteps.body: Each player chooses a monster board. Place its life dial at 10 and its star (VP) tracker at 0.

setupSteps.title: Shuffle power cards
setupSteps.body: Reveal 3 power cards face up next to the deck. Place energy cubes nearby.

setupSteps.title: Tokyo is empty to start
setupSteps.body: Nobody starts in Tokyo. The first player to roll an attack moves there.

howToPlaySteps.title: Roll dice up to 3 times
howToPlaySteps.body: Roll all 6 dice. Keep any you like and re-roll the rest. You can re-roll twice for a total of 3 throws.

rules.title: Hearts heal
rules.body: Each heart restores 1 health (but not while you're in Tokyo).

rules.title: Claws attack
rules.body: Claws damage every monster NOT in your location. If you're in Tokyo, you hit everyone outside; if you're outside, you hit whoever is in Tokyo.

rules.title: Energy buys cards
rules.body: Energy cubes fuel power cards from the market.

rules.title: Numbers score VP
rules.body: Three of a kind in 1/2/3 = 1/2/3 VP, plus 1 VP per extra of that number.

howToPlaySteps.title: Tokyo movement
howToPlaySteps.body: If you damage a monster in Tokyo, they choose to yield. If they leave, you must enter (and gain 1 VP).
howToPlaySteps.warning: You can't heal while in Tokyo. Hearts are wasted there.

turnFlow.name: Roll dice
turnFlow.description: Roll all 6, re-roll up to twice.

turnFlow.name: Resolve dice
turnFlow.description: Apply hearts, claws, energy, and numbers in any order.

turnFlow.name: Buy power cards
turnFlow.description: Spend energy on cards (1 VP discard to refresh the lineup).

scoring.summary: Score VP from dice combos, entering or staying in Tokyo, and from many power cards.
points: Start a turn in Tokyo: 2 VP
scoring.gameEnd: Win by being the last monster alive or by reaching 20 VP.

faq.question: Can I refuse to enter Tokyo if it's empty?
faq.answer: No — if you roll any claws while it's empty, you must enter and gain 1 VP.

commonMistakes.title: Healing in Tokyo
commonMistakes.body: Hearts have no effect while you occupy Tokyo. Use those slots for something else.

sections.title: Dice faces
items: Claw: attack opposite side of Tokyo
1 / 2 / 3: score with three of a kind

sections.title: Tokyo VP
items: Start a turn in Tokyo: +2 VP
